name: Shakti OBE: modulated 40 Hz (obe45), right hemisphere
origin: Todd Murphy, 8 Coil Shakti OBE recipe
summary: Murphy's OBE recipe for the 8 Coil Shakti with the 'modulated 40 Hz' (obe45) signal: 30 min over the right hemisphere, in front of and below the right ear and over the right angular gyrus, then sleep about an hour later. Murphy reports that most OBEs came during that later sleep.
setting: Lie down in a dark, quiet room. Murphy reports that most OBEs came when users fell asleep about 1 h (or 90 min) after a session, so plan to go to sleep then and use your OBE exercises; he expects it to work more often in 'right-hemispheric' people.
schedule: Vendor rules: at most once a week or every 72 h, never on consecutive days; a series of up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: Murphy's placement: 'sessions over the right hemisphere (temporal lobes, parietal lobes or the area behind the parietal lobes)', or two coils, 'one coil in front of and below the right ear, and one coil over the angular gyrus on the right side'. Here six coils cover those two spots, FT10 and T10 in front of and below the right ear, TP8, CP6, P6 and P8 around the right angular gyrus (the site names are an inference); all six play together and channels 7-8 stay silent. 30 min, one phase. The obe45 file is proprietary; the vendor says it 'has a constant tone' and that 'the correct calibration will be 10mG for either channel, when measured from one coil' (10 mG = 1 µT, the default here). It is approximated by a continuous 40 Hz carrier whose phase swings up to 3 rad ahead of and behind a steady 40 Hz every 2 s (about 38.5 to 41.5 Hz), in 1-ms points. The right angular gyrus is where Blanke et al. 2002 evoked an OBE with implanted electrodes at far higher currents; weak-field effects there are untested. Vendor cautions: word-finding trouble means stop using the signal, and 'There is no such thing as a pushbutton technology for OBEs.' Right-hemisphere-only sessions can bring fear or unease. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop at once on fear or any distress. Independent double-blind tests found no effect of God-Helmet-type fields (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
